text: In 1876, Queen Victoria was proclaimed Empress of India.
Under the Raj, India got railways, telegraph lines, universities, and a new class of English-educated
The first passenger train ran in 1853, from Bombay to Tani.
Remember the railway that buried the bricks of Harappa?
But the railways were built mainly to carry raw cotton to the ports and British factory
cloth back in. India, once the world's great cloth maker, now bought its cloth from Manchester.
And famines kept coming. In the great famine of 1876, millions died while grain was still
being exported. An Indian thinker named Dada Bhai Naoroji added up the numbers and gave
it a name, the drain of wealth, money flowing out of India, year after year. Remember that
quarter of the world's economy? By 1950, India's share had fallen to about 4%. The
shop wasn't just unlocked, it was emptied. But the same schools and newspapers the British
built gave Indians the tools to fight back, not with swords this time, with ideas.
